title: watch sizes the pane once; a mid-run resize draws later frames at stale size
body:
watchLive reads watchTerminalSize once at start and never re-reads it in the redraw loop, so resizing the terminal while a watch runs makes every later frame — dashboard, feed view and tick view alike — draw at the stale width and height: lines wrap, the block pushes down rows the redraw's cursor arithmetic does not know about, and the next frame draws over its own rows. The renderer seams all fit whatever size they are handed; the gap is at the size seam, so the fix shape is re-reading the size in the redraw loop (and re-clamping the feed view's scroll to the new height), not another truncation.
evidence: internal/cli/watch.go:693-695 (size read once before the draw loop; no SIGWINCH handling and no per-frame re-read anywhere in watch.go)
